description: Atlassian API token paired with the user's email — the two together make up the basic-auth credential for every Cloud REST endpoint (Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management). The email is metadata (never stored as a secret); the token is the value devboy holds.

variants.description: Cloud-only API token (`ATATT3xFf...`). Authenticates as the issuing user against Jira / Confluence / JSM via basic auth where username = the user's Atlassian email and password = this token. Self-managed Server / DC instances use Personal Access Tokens (`PATs`) instead — that's a separate variant.
variants.format_hint: starts with `ATATT` (Atlassian's prefix), variable-length tail of [A-Za-z0-9_-]

steps: Sign in with your Atlassian account
Pick a label describing where the token will live
Copy the value — shown once and never again
retrieval.notes: API tokens follow the user, not a project. Revoking one breaks every integration that authenticates as you. The matching email is set via `JIRA_EMAIL` (or `<provider>_USER` etc) — devboy treats those as metadata and skips them via the suffix list.

rotation.notes: Atlassian API tokens cannot be rotated in place. Create a new token from the same page, update every consumer (the email stays the same — only the token changes), then Revoke the old one. Revocation is immediate. Since 2024 Atlassian enforces a 1-year max lifetime, so a lapsed token is a hard 401 — rotate before the expiry email lands.

variants.display_name: Jira Server / DC Personal Access Token
variants.description: On-prem Jira Server / Data Center variant. PAT issued under user identity, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Cloud customers should use the API-token variant above.
variants.format_hint: opaque alnum string (length and prefix are server-version dependent)

steps: Open your Jira Server / DC profile → Personal Access Tokens
Pick a name + expiration (Server enforces an admin-set max)
retrieval.notes: Server / DC PATs are NOT cross-compatible with Cloud — using one against api.atlassian.com authenticates as `null`. Pick the right variant for the deployment style.

rotation.notes: Server / DC PATs cannot be rotated in place. Create a fresh token from your profile, swap consumers, then revoke the old. The instance admin may have pinned a max lifetime — if so the token hard-expires regardless of the framework cadence, so treat the admin-set limit as the real rotation deadline.
